correctness.rationale: The theorem fixes full-cross-ratio Hilbert distance (not the half normalization), a nondegenerate d=m-1 simplex for m>=2, and Euclidean-uniform point sampling. Centered log-softmax coordinates turn H into a variation norm and give strictly log-concave analytic density f(y) proportional to (sum exp y_i)^(-m). Prekopa convolution with the centered norm ball makes Euclidean ball volume log-concave and permutation symmetric; any second maximizer would force constancy along a ray by log concavity and analyticity, contradicting decay. The expected distance is convex and symmetric; the source provides an explicit positive-measure strict Jensen swap witness proving uniqueness of the median. Dirichlet exponential coordinates give center distance as log(max E/min E), yielding an exact beta product, endpoints and mean; two independent samples yield iid logistic log(E_i/F_i), their order-statistic range integral, mean 2H_{m-1} and independent extreme-value Gumbels. Independent checks gave CDF 1/2 at m=2,q=3 and rational product values at m=3,10. The source script verifies 167 diagnostics but the analytic theorems handle all m, not finite sampling.
